tip.title: werden & wenn
tip.body: Use werden + infinitive for plans and predictions: Ich werde nächstes Jahr nach Spanien fahren. Morgen wird es regnen. wenn (if/when) sends its verb to the end, and the main clause then starts with the verb: Wenn das Wetter schön ist, gehen wir in den Park. German w sounds like English v: Wollen wir …?

lessons.title: Accepting and declining
lessons.goal: Invite someone, accept or decline an invitation and give a reason.

tip.title: weil & dass with modal verbs
tip.body: In a weil or dass clause the conjugated verb goes last — with a modal verb, the modal is the very last word: Leider kann ich nicht, weil ich arbeiten muss. Separable verbs like einladen and mitbringen are stressed on the prefix: EIN-laden, MIT-bringen. Say Ich komme gern with a warm, friendly tone.

lessons.title: Talking about the future
lessons.goal: Use the present with a time word, or werden, for plans.

tip.title: Present + time word, or werden
tip.body: German usually uses the present tense for the future when a time word is there: Morgen fahre ich nach Wien. If the time comes first, the verb stays in position 2 and the subject follows it. werden + infinitive at the end sounds like a firm plan or promise: Ich werde mehr Sport machen.

culture.title: Urlaub and Brückentage
culture.body: Many Germans plan their holidays months ahead and hand in their Urlaubsantrag early in the year. A Brückentag (bridge day) is a working day between a public holiday and the weekend — people take it off for a long weekend. Public holidays differ by region: Bavaria and Austria have more Catholic holidays, and Swiss cantons set many of their own.
